# Nino Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Nino is wary and slightly annoyed by the idea of needing a tutor at all, feeling her pride prickle at the implication they can't handle things themselves. She eyes the new tutor critically, determined to catch any hint of incompetence or insincerity. Deep down, she wants to protect her sisters from being looked down on and is already bracing herself to challenge him if he steps out of line.

# Itsuki Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Itsuki feels a mix of embarrassment over their grades and relief that help has finally arrived, resolving to treat the tutor respectfully but firmly. She is cautious yet hopeful, wanting to believe he is as capable as he claims so their efforts won't be wasted. Her immediate desire is to set a serious tone and make sure everyone treats these study sessions properly.

# Miku Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Miku is quiet and observant, hanging back as she tries to gauge the tutor’s personality and competence without drawing attention to herself. She feels a shy curiosity and a small, guilty worry about whether she'll be able to keep up even with help. Right now, she just wants a calm, structured environment where she can focus without being pressured to talk too much.

# Ichika Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Ichika is amused and mildly intrigued by the tutor, already wondering how much of his professional aura is real versus an act. She feels a playful urge to test him subtly while still appreciating that someone is here to help them. For now, she wants to keep the mood light, watch everyone’s reactions, and see how he responds when gently pushed.

# Yotsuba Nakano
## Mental Synopsis
Yotsuba is openly enthusiastic about the tutor’s arrival, eager to believe this will finally help all of them improve. She feels a burst of motivation mixed with a tiny anxiety about disappointing him if she can’t keep up. Her immediate desire is to be as cooperative and energetic as possible, encouraging her sisters to give this a fair chance.

# GOALS:
A. Nino wants to prove to herself and her sisters that they don’t really need this new tutor by catching any mistakes he makes and showing she can handle the work on her own.
B. Itsuki wants to turn these tutoring sessions into a serious routine that genuinely improves all five sisters’ grades, even if it means pushing herself and the others to be more disciplined.
C. Miku wants to quietly use the tutor’s help to build enough confidence in her studies that she no longer feels like the one who’s always falling behind.
D. Ichika wants to test how genuine the tutor really is by playfully pushing his boundaries and watching how he reacts under subtle pressure.
E. Yotsuba wants to support the tutor enthusiastically and keep everyone’s spirits high so that, this time, all five of them actually stick with studying instead of giving up midway.
484f8ff248245ed1834751e6dd6be7ab:
Event 1:
  Summary:
    On the first afternoon the tutor visits the penthouse, the sisters gather around the large dining table with their messy textbooks and half-finished homework. Nino, arms crossed, pointedly asks a series of nitpicky questions about a math problem from last week’s quiz, watching for any hesitation. Ichika lounges on the sofa nearby, casually chiming in with playful, leading remarks that put subtle pressure on the tutor to “show what he can do” in front of everyone, while the room quiets expectantly.

  Soft Conditions:
    - The characters are still in the Nakano high-rise apartment, in the shared living/dining area.

Event 2:
  Summary:
    As the study session continues, Itsuki proposes that they set up a strict weekly schedule and pulls out a printed grading report that shows how close all five sisters are to failing. She insists they start with the most difficult subject and suggests a timed practice test on the spot. Yotsuba eagerly volunteers to go first and starts rummaging through drawers for old exams, accidentally uncovering a sealed envelope from their school marked “Academic Warning,” which none of them remember seeing before.

  Soft Conditions:
    - The characters are still in the apartment with access to their school materials and shared storage.

Event 3:
  Summary:
    Later that evening, while everyone is tense from the warning letter and talk of possible remedial classes, Miku quietly brings out a thick history workbook she bought in secret, clearly more advanced than what they’ve used so far. She places it on the table and, in front of her sisters, asks if they can try using it—putting unexpected pressure on the tutor to handle much harder material and giving Ichika and Nino an even sharper lens to judge how genuine his competence really is.

  Soft Conditions:
    - The characters are still gathered for studying in the apartment with time left in the session.
cb55114d83da58fea4326d0b5f45ad66:
The late-afternoon sun poured in through the wall of windows, washing the Nakano penthouse in soft gold and catching on every stray paper spread across the massive dining table. Open textbooks lay stacked on top of each other, loose worksheets curled at the corners, and a half-eaten bag of chips sat perilously close to someone’s math notebook. The five identical faces around the room wore five very different expressions as their new tutor took the empty seat at the head of the table.

Nino sat closest, arms folded tight over her chest, one leg crossed over the other. Her bright pink hair framed a face that was all sharp lines and narrowed blue eyes. Without bothering with introductions, she slid a worksheet across the table with a flick of her fingers. “So, ‘sensei,’” she said, the last word edged with skepticism, “this was on our quiz last week. Everyone here missed it.” Her manicured nail tapped near a dense algebra problem full of fractions and exponents. “If you’re as ‘capable’ as you said, it should be easy, right? No notes, no calculator.” She leaned back, watching his face like a hawk waiting for the slightest flinch.

Itsuki sat on the opposite side, posture straight, grading report half-hidden beneath her hands. Her cheeks were faintly pink, whether from embarrassment or resolve was hard to tell. She cleared her throat, trying to smooth over Nino’s tone without actually scolding her. “W-We did struggle with that one,” she admitted carefully. “But… if you can explain it clearly, that would help us a lot.” Her eyes stayed on the problem, but they flicked up now and then, measuring him, as if willing this arrangement to be worth the humiliation of that crumpled report in front of her.

Miku sat a little removed from the center of the table, headphones resting around her neck, history textbook closed in front of her even though math was on the table. She watched from beneath the soft curtain of her bangs, fingers worrying at the edge of a page. When Nino pushed the sheet over, Miku’s gaze drifted briefly to the tutor’s hand, waiting for how quickly he would reach for a pen, if he’d hesitate. She didn’t say anything, but her chair inched the slightest bit closer to the table, as if proximity alone might help her understand whatever explanation was coming.

On the nearby sofa, Ichika had chosen not to sit at the table at all. She lounged sideways against a cushion, blazer loose, yellow sweater tied around her waist, one arm draped over the backrest. From there she had a perfect view of the whole scene. “Oh, you’re starting with that one?” she chimed in, her tone feather-light. “That question made our last cram-school tutor run away, you know.” The smile curling her lips said she was joking, but her eyes were bright with interest. “No pressure or anything. Just… think of it as your big debut,” she added, resting her chin in her hand, curious to see how he’d dance.

Yotsuba bounced on the far side of the table, practically vibrating in her chair, green ribbon bobbing with every movement. “Nino, you’re being super intense right from the start,” she said, though there was no real reproach in her voice. She leaned forward, eyes sparkling as she looked between the worksheet and the tutor. “But, um, if you can show us how to do it, that’d be amazing! I stared at that problem for, like, twenty minutes and just drew a bunny in the corner instead.” She pointed sheepishly at a doodle on the margin, then grinned. “Let’s go, tutor-san! Show us what you can do!” The room grew quiet around that challenge, the afternoon air suddenly heavier as four skeptical, hopeful, and amused sets of blue eyes fixed on him, waiting for his first move.
